title: Universal Green-Chemistry Workflow for RNA Extraction and Integrity Analysis
author: Abdulhadi Albaser

steps.title: Harvest Cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 500 µL of culture (OD₆₀₀ 0.8–1.0) at 7,000 rpm for 5 mins at room temperature and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Resuspend Cell Pellet
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 200 µL of autoclaved distilled water.

steps.title: Lyse Cells
steps.instruction: Add 300 µL of acidic lysis buffer (pH 5.0) and mix gently by pipetting.

substeps.instruction: Ensure buffer composition is 69.4 mM SDS, 68 mM sodium citrate dihydrate, 132 mM anhydrous citric acid, and 10 mM EDTA.

steps.title: Disrupt Cells via Boiling
steps.instruction: Incubate the mixture at 100°C for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Perform Initial Precipitation
steps.instruction: Add 150 µL of precipitation buffer (4 M NaCl with citrate/citric acid) and invert 10 times.

steps.title: Cool and Pellet
steps.instruction: Incubate the mixture on ice for 7 minutes, then centrifuge at 16,000 xg for 3 mins.

steps.title: Isolate RNA Selectively
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant to a new tube containing 0.5 M Calcium Chloride (CaCl₂) and incubate at room temperature for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Pellet RNA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 16,000 xg for 5 mins and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Wash and Dry RNA
steps.instruction: Wash the pellet with ice-cold 70% ethanol, centrifuge for 3 mins, and air dry for 10–20 mins.

steps.title: Resuspend Purified RNA
steps.instruction: Dissolve the dried RNA in 50 µL of autoclaved distilled water.

steps.title: Prepare Agarose Gel
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.8%–1.0% agarose in 5 mM Borax solution (sodium tetraborate decahydrate).

substeps.instruction: Add GelRed or Ethidium Bromide to the melted agarose before casting.

steps.title: Prepare Running Buffer
steps.instruction: Use 5 mM Borax solution as the running buffer.

steps.title: Prepare RNA Samples
steps.instruction: Mix 20 µL of RNA with 2 µL of 10X loading buffer.

substeps.instruction: Use a colorless loading buffer (no Bromophenol Blue) for sharper visualization of small 5S rRNA bands.

steps.title: Load and Run Electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Load samples directly onto the gel and run at 120 V for 25 minutes.

steps.title: Capture Gel Image
steps.instruction: Place the gel on a UV transilluminator (302 nm or 312 nm) or a blue light imaging system.

steps.title: Identify RNA Bands
steps.instruction: Analyze the gel for specific rRNA bands based on the organism.

substeps.instruction: Bacteria (GP & GN): Identify 23S rRNA (~2.9 kb) as the upper band and 16S rRNA (~1.5 kb) as the lower band.
Yeast (Eukaryotic): Identify 28S rRNA (~3.8–4.8 kb) as the upper band and 18S rRNA (~1.9–2.0 kb) as the lower band.
Small RNA: Identify 5S rRNA and tRNAs as a smaller, fainter band near the bottom.

steps.title: Assess RNA Integrity
steps.instruction: Evaluate the quality of the extracted RNA based on band intensity and appearance.

substeps.instruction: Check Ratio: In high-quality RNA, the upper band (23S/28S) intensity should be approximately twice that of the lower band (16S/18S).
Check Degradation: Look for a smear of low-molecular-weight fragments or disappearance of the 23S/28S band.
Check Contamination: Look for high-molecular-weight bands near the wells indicating genomic DNA (gDNA) contamination.
